#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Execute an external notebook copy through the existing Jupyter adapter.

The source notebook is never edited. Retain the actual output even if a cell
fails; a missing execution or an error output makes this invocation fail.
"""

import argparse
import traceback

import nbclient
import nbformat


def main():
    from pathlib import Path

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--input', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--cwd', type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.output.exists():
        raise SystemExit('Refuse to replace a prior notebook execution')
    notebook = nbformat.read(args.input, as_version=4)
    client = nbclient.NotebookClient(
        notebook, kernel_name='casdsl', timeout=None, startup_timeout=600,
        allow_errors=False, resources={'metadata': {'path': str(args.cwd)}})
    code = 0
    try:
        client.execute()
    except BaseException:
        traceback.print_exc()
        code = 1
    finally:
        nbformat.write(notebook, args.output)
    cells = [cell for cell in notebook.cells if cell.cell_type == 'code']
    executed = sum(cell.get('execution_count') is not None for cell in cells)
    errors = sum(output.get('output_type') == 'error'
                 for cell in cells for output in cell.get('outputs', []))
    print(f'Notebook: {len(notebook.cells)} cells, {len(cells)} code cells, '
          f'{executed} executed, {errors} error outputs', flush=True)
    return 1 if not cells or executed != len(cells) or errors else code


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Current-source feedback (C21/C24). Called by just loop, slow, milestone and stop.
# loop "MODULE ..." [STEM | --extension STEM ...] executes complete original inputs.
# loop --extension STEM builds the suite imports and observes that unchanged completion file.
# An explicit +Module:facet is build-only and requires a selected acceptance consumer.
# slow "REASON" MODULE... [-- acceptance arguments...] runs the same checks as an explicit long run.
# milestone "REASON" builds all original targets and freshly executes their tests and suite.
# Logs and started/finished timing records are retained under timing/logs for every invocation.
set -euo pipefail
invocation=(scripts/feedback.sh "$@")
now() { python3 -c 'import time; print(time.monotonic_ns())'; }
started=$(now)
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
limit=300
records=timing/runs.jsonl
die() { printf 'feedback: %s\n' "$*" | tee -a "$log" >&2; exit 2; }

running() {
  incontainer bash -c '
    for process in /proc/[0-9]*; do
      [[ "$(readlink "$process/cwd" 2>/dev/null)" == "$0" ]] || continue
      name=$(cat "$process/comm" 2>/dev/null)
      if [[ "$name" == lake || "$name" == lean ]]; then echo "${process#/proc/} $name"; fi
    done' "$root"
}

command=${1:-}
[[ $# -gt 0 ]] && shift
reason=
targets=()
stems=()
sources=()
build_targets=()
case "$command" in
  stop)
    source scripts/container.sh
    active=$(running)
    [[ -n "$active" ]] || { echo "no lake or lean process works in this checkout"; exit 0; }
    echo "$active"
    incontainer kill $(echo "$active" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    exit 0
    ;;
  loop|slow|milestone) ;;
  *) sed -n '2,7p' "$0" | sed 's/^# //'; exit 2 ;;
esac

# The milestone gate observes pre-existing dirt, before this run creates its evidence.
milestone_tree_status=
if [[ "$command" == milestone ]]; then
  milestone_tree_status=$(git status --porcelain)
fi
if [[ "$command" == slow || "$command" == milestone ]]; then reason=${1:-}; fi

mkdir -p timing/logs
run_dir=$(mktemp -d "timing/logs/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$command.XXXXXX")
log=$run_dir/output.log
context=$run_dir/context.json
touch "$log" "$records"

CAS_FEEDBACK_PARENT_RUN=${CAS_FEEDBACK_RUN:-}
CAS_FEEDBACK_RUN=${run_dir##*/}
CAS_FEEDBACK_CONTEXT=$context
CAS_APPLICATION_LOG_DIR=$run_dir/application
export CAS_FEEDBACK_PARENT_RUN CAS_FEEDBACK_RUN CAS_FEEDBACK_CONTEXT CAS_APPLICATION_LOG_DIR
mkdir -p "$CAS_APPLICATION_LOG_DIR"
native() {
  incontainer env CAS_FEEDBACK_RUN="$CAS_FEEDBACK_RUN" \
    CAS_FEEDBACK_CONTEXT="$CAS_FEEDBACK_CONTEXT" \
    CAS_FEEDBACK_PARENT_RUN="$CAS_FEEDBACK_PARENT_RUN" \
    CAS_APPLICATION_LOG_DIR="$CAS_APPLICATION_LOG_DIR" "$@"
}
preparation_ns=0 build_ns=0 execution_ns=0 acceptance_ns=0
build_status= execution_status= acceptance_status=
preparation_finished=false
context_pending=true
attempted=false
attempted_sources=()
finish() {
  local status=$?
  trap - EXIT
  set +e
  if [[ "$context_pending" == true ]]; then
    python3 scripts/feedback_records.py begin "$context" "$command" "$reason" "$log" \
      "${#targets[@]}" "${#stems[@]}" "${#sources[@]}" \
      "${targets[@]}" "${stems[@]}" "${sources[@]}" "${invocation[@]}" 2>&1 | tee -a "$log"
    local refresh_status=$?
    [[ "$status" -ne 0 ]] || status=$refresh_status
  fi
  if [[ "$preparation_finished" != true ]]; then preparation_ns=$(( $(now) - started )); fi
  python3 scripts/feedback_records.py finish "$records" "$context" "$status" "$limit" \
    "$(( $(now) - started ))" "$preparation_ns" "$build_ns" "$execution_ns" "$acceptance_ns" \
    "$build_status" "$execution_status" "$acceptance_status" "$attempted" "${attempted_sources[@]}"
  status=$?
  exit "$status"
}
trap finish EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM
python3 scripts/feedback_records.py begin "$context" "$command" "$reason" "$log" \
  "${#targets[@]}" "${#stems[@]}" "${#sources[@]}" \
  "${targets[@]}" "${stems[@]}" "${sources[@]}" "${invocation[@]}" 2>&1 | tee -a "$log"

source scripts/container.sh

case "$command" in
  loop)
    [[ $# -ge 1 ]] || die 'usage: just loop "<test modules>" [STEM | --extension STEM ...]'
    [[ "$1" != *$'\n'* ]] || die 'put selected test modules on one line'
    if [[ "$1" == --extension ]]; then
      targets=(+CasCatalogue.TestSuite:leanArts)
      stems=("$@")
    else
      read -r -a targets <<<"$1"
      shift
      stems=("$@")
    fi
    ;;
  slow)
    [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || die 'usage: just slow "<reason>" <module ...> [-- acceptance arguments ...]'
    reason=$1
    shift
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
      if [[ "$1" == -- ]]; then
        shift
        [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || die 'name the acceptance selection after --'
        stems=("$@")
        break
      fi
      targets+=("$1")
      shift
    done
    ;;
  milestone)
    [[ $# -eq 1 ]] || die 'usage: just milestone "<reason>"'
    reason=$1
    [[ -z "$milestone_tree_status" ]] || die 'a milestone requires a clean committed tree'
    targets=(CasCompilerTests CasRuntimeTests CasDsl CasDslTests)
    build_targets=("${targets[@]}")
    stems=(--all)
    ;;
  *) sed -n '2,7p' "$0" | sed 's/^# //'; exit 2 ;;
esac
[[ "$command" == loop || ${#reason} -ge 20 ]] || die 'state the reason in at least 20 characters'
[[ ${#targets[@]} -gt 0 ]] || die 'select at least one test module; an empty selection cannot run'

if [[ "$command" != milestone ]]; then
  for target in "${targets[@]}"; do
    if [[ "$target" == *:* ]]; then
      [[ ${#stems[@]} -gt 0 && "$target" == +* ]] ||
        die 'an explicit +Module:facet is build-only and needs a selected acceptance consumer'
      build_targets+=("$target")
      continue
    fi
    module=${target#+}
    if [[ "$module" == *.lean ]]; then module=${module#./}; module=${module%.lean}; module=${module//\//.}; fi
    [[ "$module" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*([.][A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*$ ]] ||
      die "not a local Lean module: $target"
    case "$module" in
      CasCompiler|CasRuntime|CasCompilerTests|CasRuntimeTests|CasDsl|CasDslTests|CasCatalogue|CasGates|CasAcceptance|CasTools)
        die "$module is an aggregate; name the actual test module for a focused run" ;;
    esac
    file=${module//.//}.lean
    sources+=("$file")
    build_targets+=("+$module:deps")
  done
fi

# Preserve parsed fields on the same pending run before any native setup starts.
python3 scripts/feedback_records.py begin "$context" "$command" "$reason" "$log" \
  "${#targets[@]}" "${#stems[@]}" "${#sources[@]}" \
  "${targets[@]}" "${stems[@]}" "${sources[@]}" "${invocation[@]}" 2>&1 | tee -a "$log"
active=$(running)
[[ -z "$active" ]] || die "a run is in progress in this checkout (just stop stops it): $active"
if [[ ${#stems[@]} -gt 0 && -f .tmp/accept-run.json ]]; then
  mv .tmp/accept-run.json "$run_dir/prior-accept-run.json"
fi
if [[ ${#stems[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  python3 scripts/acceptance_inputs.py "$run_dir/selected-inputs.json" "${stems[@]}" \
    2>&1 | tee -a "$log"
fi

if [[ "$command" == milestone ]]; then
  # Lean's native header parser is also used by Lake; it does not elaborate imported tests.
  # https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/blob/v4.33.0/src/Lean/Elab/ParseImportsFast.lean
  native lake env lean --deps-json CasCompilerTests.lean CasRuntimeTests.lean CasDslTests.lean \
    > "$run_dir/imports.json" 2> >(tee -a "$log" >&2)
  python3 - "$run_dir/imports.json" > "$run_dir/sources" <<'PY'
import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
roots = ("CasCompilerTests", "CasRuntimeTests", "CasDslTests")
results = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())["imports"]
if len(results) != len(roots):
    raise SystemExit("the native import query did not return every test aggregate")
sources = []
for root, result in zip(roots, results, strict=True):
    if result["errors"] or "result" not in result:
        raise SystemExit(f"cannot discover tests of {root}: {result['errors']}")
    imports = result["result"]["imports"]
    selected = [entry["module"] for entry in imports if entry["module"] != "Init"]
    if not selected:
        raise SystemExit(f"test aggregate {root} selected no modules")
    for module in selected:
        path = Path(module.replace(".", "/") + ".lean")
        if not path.is_file():
            raise SystemExit(f"test aggregate {root} imports missing local source {path}")
        if str(path) not in sources:
            sources.append(str(path))
print("\n".join(sources))
PY
  mapfile -t sources < "$run_dir/sources"
fi

# Resolve the actual package paths in the build environment, including container symlinks.
native python3 scripts/feedback_records.py context "$context" "$command" "$reason" "$log" \
  "${#targets[@]}" "${#stems[@]}" "${#sources[@]}" \
  "${targets[@]}" "${stems[@]}" "${sources[@]}" "${invocation[@]}"
context_pending=false
preparation_ns=$(( $(now) - started ))
preparation_finished=true

# A missing local consumer retires earlier acceptance results and records this failure.
for file in "${sources[@]}"; do
  [[ -f "$file" ]] || {
    printf 'feedback: no local source for selected consumer: %s\n' "$file" | tee -a "$log" >&2
    exit 2
  }
done

# A newer explicit slow run of this exact selection and tuple supersedes older loop evidence.
if [[ "$command" == loop ]]; then
  python3 - "$records" "$context" "$limit" <<'PY'
import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
records, context, limit = sys.argv[1:]
current = json.loads(Path(context).read_text())
previous = None
for line in Path(records).read_text().splitlines():
    entry = json.loads(line)
    if entry.get("kind") in ("loop", "slow") and entry.get("attempted") and entry.get("workload") == current["workload"]:
        previous = entry
if previous and previous["seconds"] > int(limit):
    raise SystemExit(f"this exact workload last took {previous['seconds']:.3f} s; repair its cost or use an explicit long run")
PY
fi

# One phase uses one command; preserve both command failure and a failed durable-log write.
step() {
  local phase=$1 source=$2 before elapsed result
  shift 2
  printf '[%s] ' "$phase" | tee -a "$log"
  printf '%q ' "$@" | tee -a "$log"
  printf '\n' | tee -a "$log"
  attempted=true
  before=$(now)
  python3 scripts/feedback_records.py step-start "$context" "$phase" "$source" "$before" \
    "$(( preparation_ns + build_ns ))" "$@" || return $?
  set +e
  "$@" 2>&1 | tee -a "$log"
  local codes=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")
  set -e
  elapsed=$(( $(now) - before ))
  result=${codes[0]}
  [[ "$result" -ne 0 ]] || result=${codes[1]}
  python3 scripts/feedback_records.py step-finish "$context" "$before" "$elapsed" "$result" || return $?
  case "$phase" in
    build) build_ns=$(( build_ns + elapsed )); build_status=$result ;;
    execution) execution_ns=$(( execution_ns + elapsed ));
      [[ -n "$execution_status" && "$execution_status" -ne 0 ]] || execution_status=$result ;;
    acceptance) acceptance_ns=$(( acceptance_ns + elapsed )); acceptance_status=$result ;;
  esac
  return "$result"
}

status=0
# Lake retains complete failed-job logs and build progress at this threshold. The fresh
# consumer's own stdout/stderr remains unfiltered; successful import warnings stay in Lake.
step build "" native lake --log-level=error build "${build_targets[@]}" || status=$?
if [[ "$status" -eq 0 || "$command" == milestone ]]; then
  for file in "${sources[@]}"; do
    attempted_sources+=("$file")
    if step execution "$file" native lake --log-level=error lean "$file" -- -DstderrAsMessages=false; then :; else
      result=$?
      [[ "$status" -ne 0 ]] || status=$result
      [[ "$command" == milestone ]] || break
    fi
  done
fi
if [[ ${#stems[@]} -gt 0 && ( "$status" -eq 0 || "$command" == milestone ) ]]; then
  if step acceptance "" scripts/accept_files.sh "${stems[@]}"; then :; else
    result=$?
    [[ "$status" -ne 0 ]] || status=$result
  fi
fi
exit "$status"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Durable timing records shared by the existing feedback and acceptance commands."""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
import platform
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path


def read_json(path: Path) -> dict:
    return json.loads(path.read_text())


def utc() -> str:
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()


def digest(path: Path) -> str | None:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() if path.is_file() else None


def atomic_json(path: Path, value: dict) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", dir=path.parent, delete=False) as output:
        temporary = Path(output.name)
        json.dump(value, output, ensure_ascii=False)
        output.write("\n")
        output.flush()
        os.fsync(output.fileno())
    os.replace(temporary, path)


def append_record(path: Path, value: dict) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("a") as output:
        fcntl.flock(output, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        output.write(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        output.flush()
        os.fsync(output.fileno())


def identity(context: dict) -> dict:
    return {key: context.get(key) for key in (
        "run", "kind", "revision", "context", "context_status", "parent_run",
        "environment", "workload", "inputs", "log")}


def begin(argv: list[str]) -> None:
    out, kind, reason, log = argv[1:5]
    target_count, stem_count, source_count = map(int, argv[5:8])
    cursor = 8
    targets = argv[cursor:cursor + target_count]
    cursor += target_count
    stems = argv[cursor:cursor + stem_count]
    cursor += stem_count
    sources = argv[cursor:cursor + source_count]
    cursor += source_count
    selection = {"reason": reason, "targets": targets, "acceptance": stems, "sources": sources,
                 "inputs": {source: digest(Path(source)) for source in sources}}
    current = {"kind": kind, "run": Path(out).parent.name, "context": out,
               "log": log, "command": argv[cursor:]}
    if Path(out).exists():
        context = read_json(Path(out))
        if context["context_status"] != "pending" or any(
                context.get(key) != value for key, value in current.items()):
            raise ValueError("a pending feedback selection changed its original run identity")
        context.update(selection)
        atomic_json(Path(out), context)
        return
    context = {
        "utc": utc(), "started_monotonic_ns": time.monotonic_ns(),
        **current, **selection, "context_status": "pending",
        "revision": subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip(),
        "parent_run": os.environ.get("CAS_FEEDBACK_PARENT_RUN"),
        "environment": {"host": platform.node(), "system": platform.platform(),
                        "machine": platform.machine(), "python": platform.python_version()},
    }
    atomic_json(Path(out), context)
    append_record(Path(out).parent / "events.jsonl",
                  {**identity(context), "event": "run.started", "utc": context["utc"]})


def capture_context(argv: list[str]) -> None:
    import datetime, hashlib, json, os, platform, subprocess, sys
    from pathlib import Path
    out, kind, reason, log = argv[1:5]
    target_count, stem_count, source_count = map(int, argv[5:8])
    cursor = 8
    targets = argv[cursor:cursor + target_count]
    cursor += target_count
    stems = argv[cursor:cursor + stem_count]
    cursor += stem_count
    sources = argv[cursor:cursor + source_count]
    cursor += source_count
    digest = lambda data: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    def git_state(path: Path) -> dict[str, str | bool | list[str] | dict[str, str]]:
        def git(*args: str) -> bytes:
            return subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(path), *args])
        revision = git("rev-parse", "HEAD").decode().strip()
        selection = ["--", ".", ":(exclude)timing"]
        diff = git("diff", "--binary", "HEAD", *selection)
        untracked = git("ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z", *selection).decode().split("\0")
        extra = {name: digest((path / name).read_bytes()) for name in untracked if name and (path / name).is_file()}
        return {"path": str(path.resolve()), "revision": revision, "diff_sha256": digest(diff),
                "changed": git("diff", "--name-only", "HEAD", *selection).decode().splitlines(),
                "untracked": extra, "dirty": bool(diff or extra)}
    checkout = Path.cwd()
    manifest_path = checkout / "lake-manifest.json"
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())
    resolution = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(
        ["lake", "--log-level=error", "run", "feedback-context"], text=True))
    resolved = resolution["packages"]
    if not resolved or Path(resolved[0]["path"]).resolve() != checkout.resolve():
        raise SystemExit("Lake's resolved workspace does not match this checkout")
    manifest_packages = {package["name"].strip("«»"): package for package in manifest["packages"]}
    dependencies = []
    for package in resolved[1:]:
        name = package["name"]
        path = Path(package["path"]).resolve()
        declared = manifest_packages.get(name)
        declared_path = None
        if declared is not None:
            declared_path = ((checkout / declared["dir"]) if declared["type"] == "path" else
                (checkout / manifest.get("packagesDir", ".lake/packages") / name
                 / (declared.get("subDir") or ""))).resolve()
        configuration = Path(package["configuration"])
        dependencies.append({"name": name, "key": package["key"],
            "manifest_pin": declared.get("rev") if declared else None,
            "manifest_path": str(declared_path) if declared_path else None,
            "matches_manifest_path": path == declared_path,
            "configuration": str(configuration.resolve()),
            "configuration_sha256": digest(configuration.read_bytes()), **git_state(path)})
    inputs = sources.copy()
    from acceptance_inputs import CHECKPOINT, parse_selection
    acceptance_manifest, acceptance = parse_selection(stems)
    if acceptance_manifest is not None:
        inputs.append(acceptance_manifest)
    inputs += [item["source"] for item in acceptance]
    if any(item["kind"] == "extension" for item in acceptance):
        inputs.append(str(CHECKPOINT))
    inputs += ["lean-toolchain", "lake-manifest.json", "lakefile.lean"]
    # Match CasRuntime.installedManifest, including the absent-default observation.
    installed = Path(os.environ.get("CAS_LEAVES", ".lake/packages/cas_leaves"))
    if installed.suffix != ".json":
        installed /= "leaves.json"
    inputs.append(str(installed))
    if "CAS_REALIZATION_PROFILE" in os.environ:
        inputs.append(os.environ["CAS_REALIZATION_PROFILE"])
    input_hashes = {name: digest(Path(name).read_bytes()) if Path(name).is_file() else None for name in inputs}
    source = git_state(checkout)
    environment = {"host": platform.node(), "system": platform.platform(), "machine": platform.machine(),
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "lean": subprocess.check_output(["lean", "--version"], text=True).strip(),
        "lake": subprocess.check_output(["lake", "--version"], text=True).strip(),
        "selectors": {key: os.environ[key] for key in ("ELAN_TOOLCHAIN", "LEAN_PATH", "LEAN_SYSROOT",
            "CAS_LEAVES", "CAS_REALIZATION_PROFILE", "CAS_LEAF_CONTRACT_PATH", "CAS_SAGE_PYTHON",
            "CAS_GAP_PYTHON") if key in os.environ}}
    workload = {"targets": targets, "acceptance": stems, "inputs": input_hashes,
                "source": source, "dependencies": dependencies, "resolution": resolution,
                "environment": environment}
    entry = {"utc": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(), "kind": kind,
        "run": Path(out).parent.name, "revision": source["revision"], "dirty": source["dirty"],
        "reason": reason, "command": argv[cursor:], "sources": sources, "log": log,
        "workload": digest(json.dumps(workload, sort_keys=True).encode()), **workload}
    prior = read_json(Path(out))
    entry["utc"] = prior["utc"]
    entry["started_monotonic_ns"] = prior["started_monotonic_ns"]
    entry["parent_run"] = prior.get("parent_run")
    entry["context"] = out
    entry["context_status"] = "complete"
    atomic_json(Path(out), entry)
    append_record(Path(out).parent / "events.jsonl",
                  {**identity(entry), "event": "run.context", "context_status": "complete"})

def step_start(argv: list[str]) -> None:
    context_file, phase, source, started, shared = argv[1:6]
    context = read_json(Path(context_file))
    record = {
        **identity(context), "event": "module.started" if phase == "execution" else "phase.started",
        "phase": phase, "step": f"{phase}:{started}", "utc": utc(),
        "started_monotonic_ns": int(started), "source": source or None,
        "module": source.removesuffix(".lean").replace("/", ".") if source else None,
        "input_sha256": digest(Path(source)) if source else None,
        "command": argv[6:], "shared_setup_seconds": int(shared) / 1e9,
        "shared_setup": {"context": context_file, "phases": ["preparation", "build"]},
        "seconds": None, "inclusive_seconds": None, "status": None, "complete": False,
    }
    run = Path(context_file).parent
    atomic_json(run / "steps" / f"{started}.json", record)
    append_record(run / "events.jsonl", record)
    if phase == "execution":
        append_record(Path("timing/modules.jsonl"), record)


def step_finish(argv: list[str]) -> None:
    context_file, started, elapsed, status = argv[1:5]
    path = Path(context_file).parent / "steps" / f"{started}.json"
    record = read_json(path)
    seconds = int(elapsed) / 1e9
    record.update({
        "event": "module.finished" if record["phase"] == "execution" else "phase.finished",
        "finished_utc": utc(), "seconds": seconds, "status": int(status), "complete": True,
        "inclusive_seconds": seconds + record["shared_setup_seconds"],
        "final_input_sha256": digest(Path(record["source"])) if record["source"] else None,
    })
    atomic_json(path, record)
    append_record(path.parent.parent / "events.jsonl", record)
    if record["phase"] == "execution":
        append_record(Path("timing/modules.jsonl"), record)


def collect_computations(context_file: Path, shared_setup_seconds: float) -> dict:
    """Derive records only from the statement runner's durable events, never report rows."""
    context = read_json(context_file)
    run = context_file.parent
    computations: dict[str, dict] = {}
    children: dict[tuple[str, int], dict] = {}
    files: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    session_workers: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    beginnings: dict[tuple[str, int], dict] = {}
    malformed: list[str] = []
    invalid_sessions: set[str] = set()
    logs = sorted((run / "application").glob("*.jsonl"))
    for log in logs:
        expected_sequence = 0
        log_session = None
        for line_number, line in enumerate(log.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
            try:
                event = json.loads(line)
                name, data = event["event"], event["data"]
                session = event["session"]
                if not isinstance(name, str) or not isinstance(data, dict):
                    raise ValueError("invalid diagnostic event payload")
                if not isinstance(session, str) or not session:
                    raise ValueError("invalid diagnostic session")
                if (type(event["sequence"]) is not int or event["sequence"] < 0
                        or type(event["monotonicMilliseconds"]) is not int
                        or event["monotonicMilliseconds"] < 0
                        or not isinstance(event["parents"], list)
                        or any(type(parent) is not int or not 0 <= parent < event["sequence"]
                               for parent in event["parents"])):
                    raise ValueError("invalid diagnostic event ancestry or clock")
                issues = []
                if event["sequence"] != expected_sequence:
                    issues.append(f"diagnostic sequence {event['sequence']} follows {expected_sequence - 1}")
                if log_session is None:
                    log_session = session
                    if name != "session.started" or event["sequence"] != 0:
                        issues.append("the diagnostic stream has no original session header")
                elif session != log_session:
                    issues.append("the diagnostic stream changed its original session")
                    invalid_sessions.add(log_session)
                if name == "session.started" and event["sequence"] != 0:
                    issues.append("the diagnostic stream repeated its session header")
                if issues:
                    invalid_sessions.add(session)
                    malformed.extend(f"{log}:{line_number}: {issue}" for issue in issues)
                # Keep subsequent actual events after a gap; incompleteness must not erase
                # the terminal outcomes, elapsed work or source evidence that did survive.
                expected_sequence = event["sequence"] + 1
                if name == "session.started":
                    worker = data.get("feedbackWorker")
                    if worker is not None and (not isinstance(worker, str) or not worker):
                        raise ValueError("invalid declared feedback worker")
                    session_workers[session] = worker
                elif name == "file.begin":
                    if not isinstance(data["file"], str) or not data["file"]:
                        raise ValueError("invalid original file name")
                    beginnings[(session, event["sequence"])] = event
                elif name in {"computation.started", "computation.timing"}:
                    key = data["computation"]
                    for field in ("computation", "fileRun", "file", "sourceSha256"):
                        if not isinstance(data[field], str) or not data[field]:
                            raise ValueError(f"invalid computation {field}")
                    if type(data["ordinal"]) is not int or data["ordinal"] < 0:
                        raise ValueError("invalid computation ordinal")
                    timing_fields = ("cumulativeSetupMilliseconds",) if name == "computation.started" else (
                        "milliseconds", "executionMilliseconds", "setupMilliseconds",
                        "cumulativeSetupMilliseconds")
                    for field in timing_fields:
                        if type(data[field]) not in (int, float) or data[field] < 0:
                            raise ValueError(f"invalid computation {field}")
                    if name == "computation.timing":
                        if (data["setupMilliseconds"] != data["cumulativeSetupMilliseconds"]
                                or data["milliseconds"] !=
                                data["executionMilliseconds"] + data["setupMilliseconds"]):
                            raise ValueError("statement timing lost its inclusive setup")
                        result = data["result"]
                        if (not isinstance(result, dict) or type(result["published"]) is not bool
                                or type(result["fails"]) is not bool
                                or not isinstance(result["kind"], str)):
                            raise ValueError("statement timing lost its actual enclosing result")
                    item = computations.setdefault(key, {"source_log": str(log), "session": session})
                    field = "start" if name == "computation.started" else "completion"
                    if field in item or item["session"] != session:
                        raise ValueError(f"duplicate or changed {name} for {key}")
                    item[field] = event
                elif name in {"statement.child.started", "statement.child.finished",
                              "statement.child.interrupted"}:
                    if name == "statement.child.started":
                        if (type(data["ordinal"]) is not int or data["ordinal"] < 0
                                or not isinstance(data["id"], str) or not data["id"]
                                or not isinstance(data["source"], str)
                                or not isinstance(data["position"], dict)
                                or type(data["precedingSetupMilliseconds"]) is not int
                                or data["precedingSetupMilliseconds"] < 0):
                            raise ValueError("invalid original nested statement or setup")
                        child_sequence = event["sequence"]
                        field = "start"
                    else:
                        if not event["parents"]:
                            raise ValueError("nested terminal event lost its owning start")
                        child_sequence = event["parents"][-1]
                        if type(data["milliseconds"]) not in (int, float) or data["milliseconds"] < 0:
                            raise ValueError("invalid nested execution time")
                        field = "completion" if name == "statement.child.finished" else "interruption"
                        if field == "completion" and (
                                not isinstance(data["kind"], str)
                                or type(data["attempted"]) is not bool
                                or type(data["staged"]) is not bool
                                or data["publication"] != "pending enclosing cell"):
                            raise ValueError("nested result lost its staged publication boundary")
                    item = children.setdefault((session, child_sequence),
                                               {"source_log": str(log), "session": session})
                    if field in item or (field != "start" and
                                         ("completion" in item or "interruption" in item)):
                        raise ValueError(f"duplicate nested {field} at {session}/{child_sequence}")
                    item[field] = event
                elif name in {"file.started", "file.finished", "file.failed"}:
                    fields = ("fileRun", "file") if name == "file.failed" else (
                        "fileRun", "file", "sourceSha256")
                    for field in fields:
                        if not isinstance(data[field], str) or not data[field]:
                            raise ValueError(f"invalid file {field}")
                    if name != "file.failed":
                        count_field = "statements" if name == "file.started" else "executed"
                        if type(data[count_field]) is not int or data[count_field] < 0:
                            raise ValueError(f"invalid file {count_field}")
                    elif data["stage"] not in {"read", "parse"} or not isinstance(data["detail"], str):
                        raise ValueError("invalid file failure boundary")
                    item = files.setdefault((session, data["fileRun"]), {})
                    field = {"file.started": "start", "file.finished": "completion",
                             "file.failed": "failure"}[name]
                    if field in item:
                        raise ValueError(f"duplicate {name} for {data['file']}")
                    item[field] = event
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as error:
                malformed.append(f"{log}:{line_number}: {error}")
                if log_session is not None:
                    invalid_sessions.add(log_session)
    worker_starts = {}
    invalid_workers = set()
    for path in (run / "steps").glob("*.json"):
        try:
            step = read_json(path)
            if not isinstance(step["phase"], str):
                raise ValueError("invalid recorded phase")
            if step["phase"].startswith("acceptance-worker"):
                worker = step["phase"].removeprefix("acceptance-worker")
                if not worker:
                    raise ValueError("an acceptance-worker start lost its declared identity")
                if worker in worker_starts:
                    invalid_workers.add(worker)
                    raise ValueError(f"duplicate original worker start for {worker}")
                started = step["started_monotonic_ns"]
                if type(started) is not int or started < 0:
                    invalid_workers.add(worker)
                    raise ValueError(f"invalid original worker start for {worker}")
                # Compare at the native log's millisecond precision, without clamping
                # a genuinely negative interval or inventing an absent start.
                worker_starts[worker] = started // 1_000_000
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as error:
            malformed.append(f"{path}: {error}")
    first_files = {}
    for (session, _), event in beginnings.items():
        worker = session_workers.get(session)
        if worker is not None:
            entered = event["monotonicMilliseconds"]
            first_files[worker] = min(first_files.get(worker, entered), entered)
    worker_setup = {}
    for worker, entered in first_files.items():
        started = worker_starts.get(worker)
        if started is None or worker in invalid_workers:
            malformed.append(f"worker {worker} has no unique recorded startup boundary")
            invalid_workers.add(worker)
        elif entered < started:
            malformed.append(f"worker {worker} entered a file before its recorded start")
            invalid_workers.add(worker)
        else:
            worker_setup[worker] = (entered - started) / 1000
    invalid_sessions.update(session for session, worker in session_workers.items()
                            if worker in invalid_workers)
    rows = []
    root_starts = {}
    for key, item in computations.items():
        start, completion = item.get("start"), item.get("completion")
        data = (completion or start)["data"]
        seconds = data["milliseconds"] / 1000 if completion else None
        agreed = start is not None and completion is not None
        if agreed:
            agreed = all(start["data"][field] == data[field] for field in
                         ("computation", "fileRun", "file", "ordinal", "sourceSha256",
                          "cumulativeSetupMilliseconds"))
            agreed = agreed and completion["monotonicMilliseconds"] >= start["monotonicMilliseconds"]
        if start and completion and not agreed:
            malformed.append(f"computation {key} changed its original statement, input, or setup")
        worker = session_workers.get(item["session"])
        shared_worker = worker_setup.get(worker) if worker is not None else 0
        row = {
            **identity(context), **item, "unit": "statement", "computation": key,
            "parent_computation": None, "root_computation": key,
            "file": data["file"], "file_run": data["fileRun"], "worker": worker,
            "ordinal": data["ordinal"], "id": data.get("id"),
            "input_sha256": data["sourceSha256"], "seconds": seconds,
            "execution_seconds": data["executionMilliseconds"] / 1000 if completion else None,
            "setup_seconds": data["cumulativeSetupMilliseconds"] / 1000,
            "shared_setup_seconds": shared_setup_seconds,
            "shared_worker_setup_seconds": shared_worker,
            "shared_setup": {"context": str(context_file), "phases": ["preparation", "build"]},
            "inclusive_seconds": (seconds + shared_setup_seconds + shared_worker
                                  if seconds is not None and shared_worker is not None else None),
            "complete": agreed and shared_worker is not None and item["session"] not in invalid_sessions,
        }
        rows.append(row)
        if start:
            root_starts[(item["session"], start["sequence"])] = row

    # A child's own scope is the final parent of its terminal event. Its ancestors
    # identify the actual file computation and containing child; source text is never a key.
    nested_parents = {}
    nested_roots = {}
    first_children = {}
    for child_key, item in children.items():
        start = item.get("start")
        if start is None:
            malformed.append(f"nested terminal event {child_key} has no original start")
            continue
        ancestors = [(item["session"], sequence) for sequence in reversed(start["parents"])]
        root_key = next((key for key in ancestors if key in root_starts), None)
        if root_key is None:
            continue  # Ordinary Session runs remain fully retained in the raw application log.
        parent_key = next((key for key in ancestors if key in children or key in root_starts), None)
        if parent_key is None:
            malformed.append(f"nested computation {child_key} lost its actual parent")
            continue
        nested_roots[child_key] = root_key
        nested_parents[child_key] = parent_key
        first_children[parent_key] = min(first_children.get(parent_key, start["monotonicMilliseconds"]),
                                         start["monotonicMilliseconds"])

    scoped_rows = dict(root_starts)
    for child_key in sorted(nested_parents):
        item = children[child_key]
        start, completion = item["start"], item.get("completion")
        terminal = completion or item.get("interruption")
        parent_key = nested_parents[child_key]
        parent = scoped_rows.get(parent_key)
        root = root_starts[nested_roots[child_key]]
        setup = None
        preflight = None
        preceding = start["data"]["precedingSetupMilliseconds"] / 1000
        if parent is not None:
            preflight = (first_children[parent_key] - parent["start"]["monotonicMilliseconds"]) / 1000
            if preflight < 0:
                malformed.append(f"nested computation {child_key} precedes its parent")
            elif parent["setup_seconds"] is not None:
                setup = parent["setup_seconds"] + preflight + preceding
        else:
            malformed.append(f"nested computation {child_key} has no recorded containing scope")
        terminal_ordered = terminal is None or terminal["monotonicMilliseconds"] >= start["monotonicMilliseconds"]
        if not terminal_ordered:
            malformed.append(f"nested computation {child_key} has a terminal event before its start")
        execution = terminal["data"]["milliseconds"] / 1000 if terminal else None
        seconds = execution + setup if execution is not None and setup is not None else None
        enclosing = root.get("completion", {}).get("data", {}).get("result")
        key = f"{item['session']}/child/{start['sequence']}"
        row = {
            **identity(context), **item, "unit": "nested_statement", "computation": key,
            "parent_computation": parent["computation"] if parent else None,
            "root_computation": root["computation"],
            "file": root["file"], "file_run": root["file_run"], "worker": root["worker"],
            "ordinal": start["data"]["ordinal"], "id": start["data"]["id"],
            "input_sha256": root["input_sha256"], "seconds": seconds,
            "execution_seconds": execution, "setup_seconds": setup,
            "enclosing_preflight_seconds": preflight, "preceding_setup_seconds": preceding,
            "shared_setup_seconds": shared_setup_seconds,
            "shared_worker_setup_seconds": root["shared_worker_setup_seconds"],
            "shared_setup": root["shared_setup"],
            "inclusive_seconds": (seconds + shared_setup_seconds + root["shared_worker_setup_seconds"]
                                  if seconds is not None and root["shared_worker_setup_seconds"] is not None else None),
            "outcome": completion["data"] if completion else None,
            "enclosing_outcome": enclosing,
            "enclosing_published": enclosing["published"] if enclosing is not None else None,
            "complete": (completion is not None and root["complete"] and setup is not None
                         and terminal_ordered),
        }
        rows.append(row)
        scoped_rows[child_key] = row

    complete = not malformed and all(row["complete"] and
        (row["session"], row["file_run"]) in files for row in rows)
    file_records = []
    recorded_beginnings = set()
    for (session, file_run), events in files.items():
        file_rows = [row for row in rows if row["session"] == session and row["file_run"] == file_run]
        starts = [row for row in file_rows if row["unit"] == "statement"]
        nested = [row for row in file_rows if row["unit"] == "nested_statement"]
        start, finish, failure = events.get("start"), events.get("completion"), events.get("failure")
        first = start or finish or failure
        file = first["data"]["file"]
        begin_key = (session, first["parents"][0]) if first["parents"] else None
        begin = beginnings.get(begin_key)
        if begin is not None:
            recorded_beginnings.add(begin_key)
        count = start["data"]["statements"] if start else None
        executed = finish["data"]["executed"] if finish else None
        matched = (failure is None and begin is not None and begin["data"]["file"] == file and
                   count is not None and count == executed == len(starts)
                   and all(row["complete"] for row in file_rows)
                   and len({row["ordinal"] for row in starts}) == len(starts))
        failure_seconds = None
        if failure is not None:
            # A classified read/parse failure is a finished attempt, including in a
            # passing negative-control module. No statement was entered or invented.
            executed = 0
            matched = (begin is not None and begin["data"]["file"] == file and
                       start is None and finish is None and not file_rows)
            if begin is not None:
                failure_seconds = (failure["monotonicMilliseconds"] -
                                   begin["monotonicMilliseconds"]) / 1000
                matched = matched and failure_seconds >= 0
        if start:
            matched = matched and all(
                row["input_sha256"] == start["data"]["sourceSha256"] for row in file_rows)
            if file in context["inputs"]:
                matched = matched and context["inputs"][file] == start["data"]["sourceSha256"]
        if start and finish:
            matched = matched and all(start["data"][field] == finish["data"][field]
                                      for field in ("file", "fileRun", "sourceSha256"))
        matched = matched and session not in invalid_sessions
        complete = complete and matched
        file_records.append({"file": file, "file_run": file_run, "session": session, "statements": count,
                             "executed": executed, "records": len(starts), "nested_records": len(nested),
                             "total_records": len(file_rows), "complete": matched,
                             "begin": begin, "failure": failure, "failure_seconds": failure_seconds})
    for key, begin in beginnings.items():
        if key not in recorded_beginnings:
            complete = False
            file_records.append({"file": begin["data"]["file"], "file_run": None,
                                 "session": key[0], "statements": None, "executed": None,
                                 "records": 0, "nested_records": 0, "total_records": 0,
                                 "complete": False, "begin": begin, "failure": None})
    # The append-only application logs already preserve started work during SIGKILL. These
    # derived records are published once by the owning run's exit handler.
    with (run / "computations.jsonl").open("w") as output:
        for row in rows:
            output.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            append_record(Path("timing/computations.jsonl"), row)
        output.flush()
        os.fsync(output.fileno())
    result = {"complete": complete, "records": len(rows),
              "top_level_records": sum(row["unit"] == "statement" for row in rows),
              "nested_records": sum(row["unit"] == "nested_statement" for row in rows),
              "files": file_records, "malformed": malformed, "logs": [str(log) for log in logs],
              "record_file": str(run / "computations.jsonl")}
    atomic_json(run / "computation-summary.json", result)
    return result


def finish_feedback(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    (records, context_file, status, limit, total, preparation, build, execution, acceptance,
     bs, es, acs, attempted) = argv[1:14]
    attempted_sources = argv[14:]
    context_path = Path(context_file)
    entry = read_json(context_path)
    seconds = int(total) / 1e9
    over = entry["kind"] == "loop" and seconds > int(limit)
    execution_result = int(status)
    result = execution_result or (1 if over else 0)
    shared = (int(preparation) + int(build)) / 1e9
    interrupted = False
    for path in (context_path.parent / "steps").glob("*.json"):
        step = read_json(path)
        if not step["complete"]:
            interrupted = True
            elapsed = (time.monotonic_ns() - step["started_monotonic_ns"]) / 1e9
            step.update({"event": "module.interrupted" if step["phase"] == "execution"
                         else "phase.interrupted", "seconds": elapsed,
                         "inclusive_seconds": elapsed + step["shared_setup_seconds"],
                         "status": execution_result or 1, "finished_utc": utc()})
            atomic_json(path, step)
            append_record(context_path.parent / "events.jsonl", step)
            if step["phase"] == "execution":
                append_record(Path("timing/modules.jsonl"), step)
    for source in entry["sources"]:
        if source not in attempted_sources:
            append_record(Path("timing/modules.jsonl"), {
                **identity(entry), "event": "module.not_run", "source": source,
                "module": source.removesuffix(".lean").replace("/", "."),
                "input_sha256": entry["inputs"].get(source), "seconds": None,
                "inclusive_seconds": None, "shared_setup_seconds": shared,
                "complete": False, "status": None, "run_status": execution_result,
            })
    computations = collect_computations(context_path, shared)
    if not computations["complete"]:
        result = result or 1
    entry.update({
        "seconds": seconds, "status": result, "execution_status": execution_result,
        "over_limit": over, "within_loop_bound": seconds <= int(limit),
        "attempted": attempted == "true", "attempted_sources": attempted_sources,
        "finished_utc": utc(), "complete": not interrupted, "computations": computations,
        "preparation_seconds": int(preparation) / 1e9,
        "phases": {
            **{name: {"seconds": int(elapsed) / 1e9, "status": int(code) if code else None}
               for name, elapsed, code in (("build", build, bs), ("execution", execution, es),
                                          ("acceptance", acceptance, acs))},
        },
    })
    summary = (f"{entry['kind']}: execution status {execution_result}; status {result} "
               f"in {seconds:.3f} s; log {entry['log']}")
    if over:
        summary += (f"\nOVER THE LIMIT: the {limit}-second development loop needs repair. "
                    "The run was allowed to finish.")
    with Path(entry["log"]).open("a") as output:
        output.write(summary + "\n")
    atomic_json(context_path.parent / "result.json", entry)
    append_record(Path(records), entry)
    append_record(context_path.parent / "events.jsonl",
                  {**identity(entry), "event": "run.finished", "status": result,
                   "seconds": seconds, "finished_utc": entry["finished_utc"]})
    print(summary)
    return result


if __name__ == "__main__":
    command = sys.argv[1]
    arguments = [sys.argv[0], *sys.argv[2:]]
    if command == "begin":
        begin(arguments)
    elif command == "context":
        capture_context(arguments)
    elif command == "step-start":
        step_start(arguments)
    elif command == "step-finish":
        step_finish(arguments)
    elif command == "finish":
        raise SystemExit(finish_feedback(arguments))
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"unknown timing operation: {command}")

"""Complete native creation interfaces for original occurrence/continuation controls.

The original set-limit provider computes the target cone. This peer exercises
native record transport and owned continuations; it implements no pullback
algorithm, mathematical definition, or native proof.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from cas_port import input_ref
from cas_session import export, proxy, serve

configuration = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
creation_count = 0


def observe(label, context, captures):
    record = {
        "label": label,
        "prepared_role": context.get("prepared_role"),
        "kind": context.get("kind"),
        "arguments": context.get("arguments", []),
        "parameter_count": len(context.get("parameters", [])),
        "captures": [value.reference() for value in captures],
    }
    with Path(configuration["log"]).open("a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
        log.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")


def native_interface(label, captures):
    """Lease the actual native interface; every later use keeps its supplied inputs."""

    def invoke(context):
        assert context["kind"] == "dependent"
        observe(label, context, captures)
        role = context["prepared_role"]
        if role.startswith("project:"):
            assert context["arguments"] == []
            return native_interface(label + "/" + role, captures)
        # Only actual native applications introduce these new input positions.
        assert context["arguments"]
        arguments = [proxy(input_ref(["arguments", index]))
                     for index in range(len(context["arguments"]))]
        return native_interface(label + "/application", [*captures, *arguments])

    return export(invoke, captures)


def creation(context):
    global creation_count
    assert context["prepared_role"] == ""
    assert context["arguments"] == []
    assert context["argument_layouts"] == []
    assert context["bindings"] == []
    parameters = context["parameters"]
    assert len(parameters) >= 4
    diagram = parameters[3]
    assert diagram["ctor"] == "cospan" and len(diagram["args"]) == 2
    # The diagram packet is structural; its original declared fields are typed
    # inputs. No invented whole-D reference or fixed source constant is decoded.
    captures = [proxy(input_ref(["parameters", index])) for index in (0, 1, 2)]
    captures.extend(proxy(input_ref(["parameters", 3, "args", index])) for index in range(2))
    captures.extend(proxy(input_ref(["parameters", index])) for index in range(4, len(parameters)))
    mode = ("inline", "owned", "repeat", "missing")[min(creation_count, 3)]
    creation_count += 1
    observe("creation:" + mode, context, captures)
    if mode == "owned":
        return native_interface("complete-created-root", captures)

    # Original native data-field order:
    # LiftsToLimit = [LiftableCone, makesLimit]
    # LiftableCone = [liftedCone, validLift]
    # Cone = [pt, pi]; Iso = [hom, inv]. Native proof fields have no reply slot.
    cone = [native_interface("source-apex", captures),
            native_interface("source-cone-pi", captures)]
    comparison = [native_interface("validLift-hom", captures),
                  native_interface("validLift-inv", captures)]
    liftable = [cone, comparison]
    if mode == "missing":
        return [liftable]
    return [liftable, native_interface("source-makesLimit", captures)]


serve("creation-invocation-peer", "0", {
    "lift.finite_sets.pullbacks": creation,
})

"""Whole-control framing peer; it supplies no mathematical answers.

Every invocation is logged. Invalid modes place a fault after a valid first
child so a consumer must reject the complete frame before running that child.
The valid mode is used only to inspect transport admission of exact captures.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from cas_port import input_ref, read_frame, result_ref, write_frame

mode, log_name = sys.argv[1:]
log_path = Path(log_name)
write_frame({"op": "ready", "protocol": 2, "contract": "cas-computation/2",
             "features": ["scoped-values/2", "deferred/2", "suspend-resume/2",
                          "export-capture-frames/2"],
             "backend": "control-admission-peer", "backend_version": "0"})
hello = read_frame()
assert hello == {"op": "hello", "protocol": 2, "contract": "cas-computation/2"}
write_frame(dict(hello, status="ok"))
while (request := read_frame()) is not None:
    with log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as output:
        output.write(json.dumps(request, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    rid = request["request_id"]
    if request["op"] == "$cas.discard":
        write_frame({"request_id": rid, "status": "ok", "disposed": True})
        continue
    if request["op"] != "op.rings.mul":
        write_frame({"request_id": rid, "status": "error", "kind": "UnexpectedChild",
                     "message": "the whole control should have failed before this child"})
        continue
    assert set(request) == {"protocol", "request_id", "op", "input", "args", "scope_id"}
    context = request["args"]
    reference = input_ref(["parameters", 0])
    call = {"op": "op.rings.add", "input": "op.rings.add#input", "args": context}
    calls = [call]
    captures = [reference]
    exports = []
    template = result_ref(0)
    if mode == "duplicate_capture":
        captures.append(reference)
    elif mode == "bad_export_capture":
        exports = [{"token": "local-export", "captures": [reference, reference]}]
    elif mode == "bad_later_call":
        calls.append(dict(call, owner="provider-claimed-owner"))
    elif mode == "bad_later_graph":
        calls.append({"op": "$cas.project", "args": {"value": reference, "field": 0,
                                                       "resultType": "provider-claimed-type"}})
    elif mode == "bad_template_scope":
        template = {"ctor": "scopeRef", "args": [999999]}
    elif mode == "undeclared_opaque":
        calls.append(dict(call, args={"ctor": "opaqueData", "args": ["foreign-token"]}))
    elif mode == "valid":
        captures = [input_ref(["first"]), input_ref(["second"])]
        exports = [{"token": "local-export", "captures": captures}]
        calls = [{"op": "$cas.project", "args": {"value": captures[0], "field": 0}}]
    else:
        raise ValueError(mode)
    if mode in ("bad_later_call", "bad_template_scope", "undeclared_opaque"):
        write_frame({"request_id": rid, "status": "ok",
                     "value": {"ctor": "deferredData", "args": [calls, template]},
                     "exports": exports})
    else:
        write_frame({"request_id": rid, "status": "suspended", "continuation": "continuation-0",
                     "captures": captures, "calls": calls, "exports": exports})

"""Protocol-v2 provider for kernel lift tests.

It answers the structural views and the prescribed restriction lift of RX-LIFT
(tests/acceptance/proposals/independent-extension-reconstruction-20261024/
completion/rx-lift-prescribed-stages.cas). Each answer is provider-owned data: a
native export, whose later projections and applications reach this process
again through `$cas.invoke_export` and are answered the same way. The operation
and invocation context of each request, export requests included, are written to
the log file named by the first argument, one JSON object per line. The kernel
test reads that log.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys

from cas_port import serve
from cas_session import JsonValue, export

LOG = sys.argv[1]


def _answer(operation: str):
    def handler(context: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
        with open(LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
            log.write(json.dumps({"op": operation, "context": context}) + "\n")
        return export(_answer(f"{operation}/export"), [])

    return handler


OPERATIONS = sys.argv[2:]

serve("kernel-lift-peer", "0", {operation: _answer(operation) for operation in OPERATIONS})

"""Protocol-v2 provider for kernel predicate tests.

It answers whether a natural number is prime. The kernel decides membership in
the subset of primes from this Boolean answer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from cas_port import point_invocation, serve
from cas_session import JsonValue


def _natural(value: JsonValue) -> int:
    """A natural operand: a returned number, or the numeral descriptor of one."""
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return value
    assert isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(value.get("args"), list), value
    number = value["args"][-1]
    assert isinstance(number, int), value
    return number


def is_prime(context: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
    fields = point_invocation(context, "mor.sets.nat_is_prime")
    number = _natural(fields[6])
    return number > 1 and all(number % divisor for divisor in range(2, number))


serve("kernel-predicate-peer", "0", {"mor.sets.nat_is_prime": is_prime})

"""Protocol-v2 traffic provider for kernel session tests.

It answers integer-ring addition and multiplication and the cardinality of a
named finite set from its complete published method invocation. A numeral operand arrives
as its registered descriptor; the peer reads its integer. Multiplication by two is
answered by a deferred published addition on the caller's own ring parameter.
The explicit fixed-group-kernel mode supplies opaque native fields and an exact
input reference for admission checks; it performs no group computation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys

from cas_port import deferred_call, deferred_data, input_ref, method_invocation, result_ref, serve
from cas_session import ComputationError, JsonValue, UnsupportedOperation, export, proxy


FIRST_ADD_FAILURE: str | None = None
LOG: str | None = None
REFERENCE_INPUTS = False
FIXED_ENDPOINT: int | None = None
if len(sys.argv) == 3 and sys.argv[1] == "--reference-add":
    REFERENCE_INPUTS = True
    LOG = sys.argv[2]
elif len(sys.argv) == 4 and sys.argv[1] == "--fixed-group-kernel" and \
        sys.argv[2] in ("left", "right"):
    FIXED_ENDPOINT = 0 if sys.argv[2] == "left" else 1
    LOG = sys.argv[3]
elif sys.argv[1:] not in ([], ["--corrupt-add"]):
    if len(sys.argv) != 4 or sys.argv[1] != "--fail-first-add" or \
            sys.argv[2] not in ("unsupported", "unavailable"):
        raise SystemExit("usage: kernel_session_peer.py "
                         "[--corrupt-add | --fail-first-add unsupported|unavailable LOG | "
                         "--reference-add LOG | --fixed-group-kernel left|right LOG]")
    FIRST_ADD_FAILURE, LOG = sys.argv[2:]


def _integer(value: JsonValue) -> int:
    """An integer operand: a returned integer, or the ring numeral descriptor of one."""
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return value
    assert isinstance(value, dict) and value["ctor"] == "num.rings", value
    arguments = value["args"]
    assert isinstance(arguments, list), value
    number = arguments[-1]
    assert isinstance(number, int), value
    return number


def _operands(context: JsonValue) -> tuple[int, int]:
    assert isinstance(context, dict)
    arguments = context["arguments"]
    assert isinstance(arguments, list)
    left, right = arguments[0]
    return _integer(left), _integer(right)


def add(context: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
    global FIRST_ADD_FAILURE
    if LOG is not None:
        with open(LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
            log.write(json.dumps({"op": "op.rings.add", "context": context}) + "\n")
    failure, FIRST_ADD_FAILURE = FIRST_ADD_FAILURE, None
    if failure == "unsupported":
        raise UnsupportedOperation("op.rings.add")
    if failure == "unavailable":
        raise ComputationError("session-failure-control", "first addition unavailable")
    left, right = _operands(context)
    # Deliberately wrong data only for the explicit proof-discharge regression.
    return left + right + (1 if "--corrupt-add" in sys.argv[1:] else 0)


def multiply(context: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
    if REFERENCE_INPUTS:
        assert LOG is not None
        with open(LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
            log.write(json.dumps({"op": "op.rings.mul", "context": context}) + "\n")
    left, right = _operands(context)
    if right != 2:
        return left * right
    assert isinstance(context, dict)
    call = dict(context)
    call["parameters"] = [input_ref(["parameters", 0])]
    # The explicit parity mode forwards the original two occurrences of the same
    # input address. The kernel owns their typed bindings and the child request.
    call["arguments"] = [[input_ref(["arguments", 0, 0]),
                          input_ref(["arguments", 0, 0])]] if REFERENCE_INPUTS else [[left, left]]
    return deferred_data(
        [deferred_call("op.rings.add", "op.rings.add#input", call)], result_ref(0)
    )


def cardinality(context: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
    assert isinstance(context, dict)
    _, actions, receiver = method_invocation(context, "meth.cardinality", "fun.sets.cardinality")
    assert actions == [{"ctor": "fun.sets.cardinality", "args": []}], actions
    assert isinstance(receiver, dict) and receiver["ctor"] == "obj.sets.fin"
    size = receiver["args"]
    assert isinstance(size, list)
    return {"ctor": "finite", "args": [size[0]]}


def group_kernel(context: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
    """Supply a whole native record, changing only its fixed original input reference."""
    assert FIXED_ENDPOINT is not None and LOG is not None
    _, actions, receiver = method_invocation(
        context, "meth.group_arrow_kernel", "fun.arrows_groups.kernel"
    )
    assert actions == [{"ctor": "fun.arrows_groups.kernel", "args": []}], actions
    assert isinstance(receiver, dict) and receiver["ctor"] == "arrow", receiver
    fields = receiver["args"]
    assert isinstance(fields, list) and len(fields) == 3, receiver
    assert fields[0] == fields[1], "the original distinct endpoints must have equal packets"
    address = ["receiver", "args", FIXED_ENDPOINT]
    with open(LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
        log.write(json.dumps({"op": "meth.group_arrow_kernel", "context": context,
                              "ambient": address}) + "\n")

    def group_field(_context: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
        raise NotImplementedError("the admission control supplies no group computation")

    # These are opaque supplied fields, as in the original fixed-result control.
    # Only the ambient is fixed by the requested source. No group equation is claimed.
    ambient = proxy(input_ref(address))
    return [export(group_field, []), ambient.reference(), export(group_field, [])]


serve(
    "kernel-session-peer",
    "0",
    {"op.rings.add": add, "op.rings.mul": multiply, "meth.cardinality": cardinality}
    | ({"meth.group_arrow_kernel": group_kernel} if FIXED_ENDPOINT is not None else {}),
)

"""Protocol-v2 provider for kernel suspension tests.

It answers integer-ring addition directly. Multiplication by two suspends: the
generator asks the kernel to resolve the published addition `a + a` on the
caller's own ring, then returns a reference to that child result on resume.
Multiplication by three suspends twice: it declares the ring parameter as a
capture of the first suspension, and the second addition takes that capture and
the first child result by their references in the resumed scope.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from cas_port import deferred_call, input_ref, serve
from cas_session import JsonValue, proxy, suspend


def _integer(value: JsonValue) -> int:
    """An integer operand: a returned integer, or the ring numeral descriptor of one."""
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return value
    assert isinstance(value, dict) and value["ctor"] == "num.rings", value
    number = value["args"][-1]
    assert isinstance(number, int), value
    return number


def _operands(context: JsonValue) -> tuple[int, int]:
    assert isinstance(context, dict)
    arguments = context["arguments"]
    assert isinstance(arguments, list)
    left, right = arguments[0]
    return _integer(left), _integer(right)


def add(context: JsonValue) -> JsonValue:
    left, right = _operands(context)
    return left + right


def multiply(context: JsonValue):
    left, right = _operands(context)
    assert right in (2, 3), context
    assert isinstance(context, dict)
    ring = proxy(input_ref(["parameters", 0]))
    call = dict(context)
    call["parameters"] = [ring.reference()]
    call["arguments"] = [[left, left]]
    results = yield suspend([deferred_call("op.rings.add", "op.rings.add#input", call)], [ring])
    if right == 2:
        return results[0].reference()
    again = dict(call)
    again["parameters"] = [ring.reference()]
    again["arguments"] = [[results[0].reference(), left]]
    results = yield suspend([deferred_call("op.rings.add", "op.rings.add#input", again)], [])
    return results[0].reference()


serve("kernel-suspension-peer", "0", {"op.rings.add": add, "op.rings.mul": multiply})

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exercise the actual notebook worker and CAS session, not a substitute executor.

The integer statements and SDK peer are the original ScopedDeclarationTests controls.
Run against the built CasDsl.Notebook prelude with the installed notebook adapter.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

from nbdsl_kernel.protocol import InspectOk
from nbdsl_kernel.worker.client import WorkerClient


def retained_integer(client: WorkerClient, name: str, expected: int, snapshot: int) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Check the actual frozen binding and value, without executing a query."""
    reply = client.inspect(name, len(name), snapshot=snapshot)
    assert isinstance(reply, InspectOk) and reply.found, reply
    assert reply.name == name and reply.details is not None, reply
    details = reply.details
    binding = details["binding"]
    assert isinstance(binding, dict), details
    runtime = details["runtime"]
    assert isinstance(runtime, dict) and runtime["hasPacket"], details
    assert runtime["packet"] == expected, details
    assert isinstance(runtime["reference"], dict), details
    source = details["source"]
    assert isinstance(source, dict) and source["nativeExpressions"], details
    assert any(row["id"] == binding and row["name"] == name
               for row in source["context"]), source
    assert isinstance(details["candidates"], list), details
    return details


def require_routines(details: dict[str, object], expected: set[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
    """The committed receipt, not the registration name, supplies the actual routines."""
    runtime = details["runtime"]
    assert isinstance(runtime, dict)
    completions = runtime["completions"]
    assert isinstance(completions, list)
    actual: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for completion in completions:
        producer = completion["producer"]
        if producer["kind"] == "kernel":
            assert not completion["routines"], completion
            continue
        assert len(completion["routines"]) == 1, completion
        frame = completion["routines"][0]
        for key in ("connection", "occurrence", "requestId"):
            assert frame[key] == producer[key], completion
        observations = frame["observations"]
        assert len(observations) == 1, frame
        routine = observations[0]
        assert routine["role"] == "entrypoint", routine
        assert routine["code_sha256"] and len(routine["code_sha256"]) == 64, routine
        actual.append((producer["target"]["operation"], routine["qualified_name"]))
    assert len(actual) == len(expected) and set(actual) == expected, actual


def run(root: Path, contract: Path) -> None:
    python = contract / ".venv/bin/python"
    assert python.is_file(), python
    peer = root / "scripts/probes/kernel_session_peer.py"
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="cas-notebook-cell-") as directory:
        manifest = Path(directory) / "leaves.json"
        manifest.write_text(json.dumps({
            "backends": [{"name": "peer", "command": str(python), "args": [str(peer)]}],
            "registrations": [
                {"operation": op, "input": op + "#input", "backend": "peer"}
                for op in ("op.rings.add", "op.rings.mul")
            ],
        }))
        previous = os.environ.get("CAS_LEAVES")
        os.environ["CAS_LEAVES"] = str(manifest)
        client = WorkerClient(root, prelude="CasDsl.Notebook", session_mode="language",
                              on_stream=lambda stream, line: print(f"[{stream}] {line}", end="", flush=True))
        try:
            print("Importing and negotiating CasDsl.Notebook", flush=True)
            ready = client.start()
            print("Negotiated", flush=True)
            nonce = ready.worker_nonce
            assert ready.protocol == 2 and nonce
            assert ready.snapshot == 0
            parent = client.execute('#cas "let outer := 17 + 29 in ℤ"', "parent")
            assert parent.status == "ok", parent
            assert parent.commit is not None
            assert parent.outputs and parent.commit.result_refs
            assert parent.worker_nonce == nonce
            committed = parent.snapshot
            assert committed is not None
            outer = retained_integer(client, "outer", 46, committed)
            require_routines(outer, {("op.rings.add", "add")})
            print("Parent committed with frozen integer observation", flush=True)

            staged = client.execute_at(
                '#cas "let localSum := outer + 1 in ℤ"\n'
                '#cas "let localProduct := localSum · 2 in ℤ"\n'
                '#cas "assert localProduct = 94 in ℤ"',
                "staged", committed,
            )
            assert staged.status == "ok", staged
            assert staged.commit is not None and staged.commit.result_refs
            assert len(staged.outputs) == 3, staged
            assert staged.parent_snapshot == committed
            assert staged.snapshot != committed
            assert staged.commit.transaction_id != parent.commit.transaction_id
            assert staged.commit.output_batch_id != parent.commit.output_batch_id
            assert len({item.result_id for item in staged.outputs}) == 3
            assert staged.snapshot is not None
            retained_integer(client, "localSum", 47, staged.snapshot)
            product = retained_integer(client, "localProduct", 94, staged.snapshot)
            require_routines(product, {("op.rings.mul", "multiply"), ("op.rings.add", "add")})
            assert retained_integer(client, "outer", 46, staged.snapshot)["binding"] == outer["binding"]
            print("Multi-command cell committed with retained values", flush=True)
